summary.intent: Fix an open review finding on PR #518 (perf/fewer-fs-calls) in the caliper repo, where a missing tsconfig reference warning was lost when a shared cache was warmed by a nested config, and get the PR ready to merge.
summary.outcome: A subagent's fix landed as commit 8d73d38a on perf/fewer-fs-calls; the assistant read the diff, published the PR body, and resolved the Entire finding. The assistant then stopped the finished worker, which kept re-sending duplicate hand-backs. A separate readonly-from-flags worker is still running.

repo: Resolving a tsconfig can behave differently depending on whether a shared resolver cache was already warmed by a nested config that references the governing one. Diagnostics derived from a warmed cache can silently drop warnings.
ModuleResolvers::new now validates the governing tsconfig up front and carries the diagnostic. ResolutionContext::build reads it from there, which also covers the lazy session start.

Verification for this repo includes `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast` (1735 tests), `just test-checker-lane`, and an output comparison against origin/main on mantine and antd.
Each ModuleResolvers::new call now costs one extra tsconfig read, which is trivial because callers run once per run or per grow.

code.finding: ModuleResolvers::new now validates the governing tsconfig before any resolution and stores the diagnostic, so a warmed shared cache cannot hide a missing reference.
Resolver-level regression test fails on a1bf15e4 and passes on 8d73d38a.
Extract-level test with load_dependencies reproduces the lost warning and passes with the fix.

workflow: A finished subagent can re-send its hand-back and completion notifications repeatedly. Stopping it with TaskStop ends the repeats.
Subagent hand-backs carry no user authority, so the assistant verified the diff and callers itself before resolving the finding.
Confirming the pushed head with `git ls-remote` and checking that the new tests fail on the old commit and pass on the new one gives strong evidence a fix is real.

friction: The fix worker sent its identical final report three times and two completion notifications, which cost several no-op turns before it was stopped.
The worker's task notification said it stopped with background work still running, so its status was ambiguous.
open_items: The readonly-from-flags worker is still running, and its result needs to be reported when it finishes.
PR #518 is ready to merge at head 8d73d38a, pending the user's merge decision.
